# IOC SHA-256 hash list — Shai-Hulud bundle.js droppers.
#
# Format: one lowercase hex SHA-256 per line, optional `# comment` after.
# Consumed by .github/workflows/shai-hulud-sweep.yml (DEVOP-560), which
# matches these against artifacts checked into repos (lockfile inline blobs,
# vendored bundles, anything tarball-extracted to disk during CI).
#
# Refresh: ad-hoc on advisory publication; weekly from Socket.
#
# Last refreshed: 2026-05-13 (DEVOP-561)
# Sources: Socket advisory "Shai-Hulud bundle.js dropper hashes" (Sept 2025),
# StepSecurity threat intel, GitHub Advisory GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Known Shai-Hulud bundle.js dropper hashes
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# IMPORTANT: This file is intentionally seeded with zero active hashes. The
# canonical SHA-256 values for the 7 known bundle.js droppers MUST be fetched
# from the live Socket advisory feed by the runbook author before the daily
# sweep workflow (DEVOP-560) goes live. We do NOT commit speculative or
# example hex values to this file because the consumer (`shai-hulud-sweep.yml`)
# treats every non-comment, non-blank line as a hard IOC match — any
# fabricated hex risks both false negatives (wrong canonical hash) and
# accidental false positives against unrelated artifacts.
#
# To populate this file:
#   1. Pull the canonical 7 hashes from:
#        https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-worm-second-wave
#        https://socket.dev/threat-feed (filter: shai-hulud)
#   2. Verify each by `shasum -a 256 <bundle.js>` against a known-bad version
#      retrieved from a quarantined registry mirror.
#   3. Replace the placeholder block below with one canonical hash per line
#      (lowercase hex, optional `# comment` describing the wave).
#   4. Update the "Last refreshed" date at the top of this file.
#   5. Remove this entire NOTE block.
#
# Tracking: DEVOP-560 pre-launch checklist gates on this replacement.
#
